service:
Amazon Polly is a web service that makes it easy to synthesize speech from text.

The Amazon Polly service provides API operations for synthesizing high-quality speech from plain text and Speech Synthesis Markup Language (SSML), along with managing pronunciations lexicons that enable you to get the best results for your application domain.

Authenticated API calls must be signed using the Signature Version 4 Signing Process. For more information, see Signing Amazon Web Services API Requests in the IAM User Guide.

operations.CreateVoice:
Creates a custom voice from recordings of a speaker and returns it in pending status. Use GetVoice to check the status. When the status is active, you can use the voice ID in SynthesizeSpeech, StartSpeechSynthesisTask, and StartSpeechSynthesisStream.

The custom-voice-max-count service quota limits the number of custom voices in your account in each Region. If you reach the quota, the request fails with ServiceQuotaExceededException.

This operation requires permissions to perform the polly:CreateVoice action. You also need s3:GetObject permission on each recording that you specify by S3Url. If you specify a customer managed key, you also need kms:DescribeKey, kms:GenerateDataKey, and kms:Decrypt permissions on the key. If you specify Tags, you also need the polly:TagResource permission.
operations.DeleteLexicon:
Deletes the specified pronunciation lexicon stored in an Amazon Web Services Region. A lexicon which has been deleted is not available for speech synthesis, nor is it possible to retrieve it using either the GetLexicon or ListLexicon APIs.

For more information, see Managing Lexicons.
operations.DeleteVoice:
Deletes a custom voice. DescribeVoices and GetVoice stop returning the voice immediately. You can't restore a deleted voice.

You can delete a voice in active or failed status. If the voice is in pending status, the request fails with ConflictException. If no custom voice with the specified ID exists in your account and Region, the request fails with ResourceNotFoundException. You can delete the voice even if you disabled its Amazon Web Services KMS key or scheduled it for deletion.

This operation requires permissions to perform the polly:DeleteVoice action.
operations.DescribeVoices:
Returns the list of voices: the voices that Amazon Polly provides and the custom voices in your account. Each voice speaks a specified language and is identified by an ID. A voice that Amazon Polly provides is either male or female, and its ID is the ASCII version of the voice name.

When synthesizing speech (SynthesizeSpeech), you provide the voice ID for the voice you want from the list of voices returned by DescribeVoices.

For example, your news reader application reads news in a specific language, and you want to give users the option to choose the voice. With the DescribeVoices operation, you can provide a list of available voices for users to choose from.

You can optionally specify a language code to filter the available voices. For example, if you specify en-US, the operation returns a list of all available US English voices.

The list includes custom voices in every status. For each voice, Origin indicates whether Amazon Polly provides the voice or you created it. You can use a custom voice for synthesis only when its status is active. A voice in failed status stays in the list until you delete it.

For a custom voice, DescribeVoices returns Origin, Id, Name, Status, LanguageCode, LanguageName, SupportedEngines, and CreationTime. To get Arn, StatusReason, VoiceCreationData, and CustomerManagedEncryption, use GetVoice.

The LanguageCode and Engine filters apply to custom voices in the same way as to voices that Amazon Polly provides.

This operation requires permissions to perform the polly:DescribeVoices action.
operations.GetLexicon: Returns the content of the specified pronunciation lexicon stored in an Amazon Web Services Region. For more information, see Managing Lexicons.
operations.GetSpeechSynthesisTask: Retrieves a specific SpeechSynthesisTask object based on its TaskID. This object contains information about the given speech synthesis task, including the status of the task, and a link to the S3 bucket containing the output of the task.
operations.GetVoice:
Returns the status and properties of a custom voice. Use this operation after CreateVoice to check whether the status of the voice is active or failed. Unlike DescribeVoices, GetVoice also returns Arn, VoiceCreationData, CustomerManagedEncryption, and StatusReason. If no custom voice with the specified ID exists in your account and Region, the request fails with ResourceNotFoundException.

This operation requires permissions to perform the polly:GetVoice action.
operations.ListLexicons: Returns a list of pronunciation lexicons stored in an Amazon Web Services Region. For more information, see Managing Lexicons.
operations.ListSpeechSynthesisTasks: Returns a list of SpeechSynthesisTask objects ordered by their creation date. This operation can filter the tasks by their status, for example, allowing users to list only tasks that are completed.
operations.ListTagsForResource: Lists the tags for an Amazon Polly resource.
operations.PutLexicon:
Stores a pronunciation lexicon in an Amazon Web Services Region. If a lexicon with the same name already exists in the region, it is overwritten by the new lexicon. Lexicon operations have eventual consistency, therefore, it might take some time before the lexicon is available to the SynthesizeSpeech operation.

Overwriting a lexicon keeps its existing tags. You can specify tags only when you create a lexicon. If you specify tags for a lexicon that already exists, the request fails with a ValidationException. To change the tags of an existing lexicon, use TagResource and UntagResource.

For more information, see Managing Lexicons.
operations.StartSpeechSynthesisStream:
Synthesizes UTF-8 input, plain text, or SSML over a bidirectional streaming connection. Specify synthesis parameters in HTTP/2 headers, send text incrementally as events on the input stream, and receive synthesized audio as it becomes available.

This operation serves as a bidirectional counterpart to SynthesizeSpeech:

  • SynthesizeSpeech

To use a custom voice, specify its ID in VoiceId. The voice must be in active status. If the voice is in pending or failed status, the request fails with ConflictException. If no custom voice with the specified ID exists in your account and Region, the request fails with ResourceNotFoundException. If the custom voice uses a customer managed key, you need kms:Decrypt permission on the key. If you disabled the key or scheduled it for deletion, the request fails with ValidationException. If you don't have permission to use the key, the request fails with AccessDeniedException. If Amazon Web Services KMS throttles Amazon Polly's request to use the key, the request fails with ThrottlingException.
operations.StartSpeechSynthesisTask:
Starts an asynchronous synthesis task by creating a new SpeechSynthesisTask. This operation requires all the standard information needed for speech synthesis, plus the name of an Amazon S3 bucket for the service to store the output of the synthesis task and two optional parameters (OutputS3KeyPrefix and SnsTopicArn). After Amazon Polly creates the synthesis task, the operation returns a SpeechSynthesisTask object that includes an identifier for the task and its current status. The SpeechSynthesisTask object is available for 72 hours after you start the asynchronous synthesis task.

To use a custom voice, specify its ID in VoiceId. The voice must be in active status. If the voice is in pending or failed status, the request fails with ConflictException. If no custom voice with the specified ID exists in your account and Region, the request fails with ResourceNotFoundException. If the custom voice uses a customer managed key, you need kms:Decrypt permission on the key. If you disable the key or schedule it for deletion before the task runs, the task fails and TaskStatusReason describes the cause.
operations.SynthesizeSpeech:
Synthesizes UTF-8 input, plain text or SSML, to a stream of bytes. SSML input must be valid, well-formed SSML. Some alphabets might not be available with all the voices (for example, Cyrillic might not be read at all by English voices) unless phoneme mapping is used. For more information, see How it Works.

To use a custom voice, specify its ID in VoiceId. The voice must be in active status. If the voice is in pending or failed status, the request fails with ConflictException. If no custom voice with the specified ID exists in your account and Region, the request fails with ResourceNotFoundException.

If the custom voice uses a customer managed key, you need kms:Decrypt permission on the key. If you disabled the key or scheduled it for deletion, the request fails with ValidationException. If you don't have permission to use the key, the request fails with AccessDeniedException. If Amazon Web Services KMS throttles Amazon Polly's request to use the key, the request fails with ThrottlingException.
operations.TagResource: Adds specified tags to a resource with the specified ARN. Existing tags on a resource are not changed if they are not specified in the request parameters. If you specify a tag key that already exists on the resource, the value in the request replaces the existing value.

AccessDeniedException.base: You don't have sufficient permissions to perform this action. For a custom voice that uses a customer managed key, Amazon Polly also returns this exception if you don't have the required Amazon Web Services KMS permissions on the key.

refs.LexiconAttributes$Alphabet: Phonetic alphabet used in the lexicon. Valid values are ipa, x-sampa, x-amazon-pinyin, x-amazon-jyutping, x-amazon-pron-kana, and x-amazon-yomigana.

refs.ListTagsForResourceInput$ResourceArn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the resource to list the tags for. You can tag Amazon Polly lexicons and custom voices.
refs.TagResourceInput$ResourceArn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the resource to add tags to. You can tag Amazon Polly lexicons and custom voices.
refs.UntagResourceInput$ResourceArn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the resource to remove tags from. You can tag Amazon Polly lexicons and custom voices.

refs.AudioEvent$AudioChunk: A chunk of synthesized audio data encoded in the format specified by the OutputFormat parameter.

AudioEvent.base: Contains a chunk of synthesized audio data.

refs.Recording$Format: The audio format of the recording: wav, flac, ogg_vorbis, or mp3. The format must match the audio data.

refs.CreateVoiceInput$ClientToken: A unique, case-sensitive identifier that you provide to ensure the idempotency of the request. If you don't specify a client token, the Amazon Web Services SDKs generate one for you. If you retry a request that succeeded with the same client token and the same parameters, Amazon Polly returns the voice that the first request created and doesn't create a second voice.

CloseStreamEvent.base: Indicates the end of the input stream. After sending this event, the input stream will be closed and all audio will be returned.

refs.StartSpeechSynthesisStreamActionStream$C: An event indicating the end of the input stream.

ConflictException.base: The request conflicts with the current state of the resource. For a custom voice, the voice isn't in the status that the operation requires. Check the status with GetVoice, and then try again.

refs.SynthesizeSpeechOutput$ContentType:
Specifies the type audio stream. This should reflect the OutputFormat parameter in your request.

  • If you request mp3 as the OutputFormat, the ContentType returned is audio/mpeg.

  • If you request ogg_vorbis as the OutputFormat, the ContentType returned is audio/ogg.

  • If you request ogg_opus as the OutputFormat, the ContentType returned is audio/ogg.

  • If you request pcm as the OutputFormat, the ContentType returned is audio/pcm in a signed 16-bit, 1 channel (mono), little-endian format.

  • If you request mu-law as the OutputFormat, the ContentType returned is audio/mulaw.

  • If you request a-law as the OutputFormat, the ContentType returned is audio/alaw.

  • If you request json as the OutputFormat, the ContentType returned is application/x-json-stream.

refs.ThrottlingReason$reason: The reason code explaining why the request was throttled.

refs.DeleteVoiceInput$VoiceId: The ID of the custom voice to delete, for example, vc-9a8fa85dd3. You can't specify the ARN of the voice.
refs.GetVoiceInput$VoiceId: The ID of the custom voice that CreateVoice returned, for example, vc-9a8fa85dd3. You can't specify the ARN of the voice.

refs.CreateVoiceInput$LanguageCode: The language of the recordings, for example, en-US. Amazon Polly doesn't detect the language from the recordings.

refs.CreateVoiceInput$Name: The name of the voice. Use the name to identify the voice in your application. The name can contain letters, digits, hyphens, and underscores, and can be up to 64 characters long. The name doesn't have to be unique. The name isn't the voice ID, which Amazon Polly assigns.

CustomerManagedEncryption.base: The customer managed key that encrypts your custom voice. If you don't specify a key, Amazon Polly encrypts the voice with an Amazon Web Services owned key.

refs.CreateVoiceInput$CustomerManagedEncrypti: The customer managed key that you want Amazon Polly to encrypt the voice with. If you omit this parameter, Amazon Polly encrypts the voice with an Amazon Web Services owned key.
refs.Voice$CustomerManagedEncryption: The customer managed key that encrypts your custom voice. CreateVoice and GetVoice return this field if you specified a key in CreateVoice.

refs.SynthesisTask$CreationTime: Timestamp for the time the synthesis task was started.
refs.Voice$CreationTime: The date and time when you created the custom voice. Voices that Amazon Polly provides don't include this field.

refs.CustomerManagedEncryption$EncryptionCont: The key-value pairs that Amazon Polly includes as the encryption context when it encrypts or decrypts the voice with the key. You can use these pairs in key policy conditions. Don't use keys that start with aws:, which are reserved.

refs.DescribeVoicesInput$Engine: Specifies the engine (standard, neural, long-form or generative) used by Amazon Polly when processing input text for speech synthesis.
refs.StartSpeechSynthesisStreamInput$Engine: Specifies the engine for Amazon Polly to use when processing input text for speech synthesis. Currently, only the generative engine is supported. If you specify a voice that the selected engine doesn't support, Amazon Polly returns an error.
refs.StartSpeechSynthesisTaskInput$Engine: Specifies the engine (standard, neural, long-form or generative) for Amazon Polly to use when processing input text for speech synthesis. Using a voice that is not supported for the engine selected will result in an error.
refs.SynthesisTask$Engine: Specifies the engine (standard, neural, long-form or generative) for Amazon Polly to use when processing input text for speech synthesis. Using a voice that is not supported for the engine selected will result in an error.
refs.SynthesizeSpeechInput$Engine: Specifies the engine (standard, neural, long-form, or generative) for Amazon Polly to use when processing input text for speech synthesis. Provide an engine that is supported by the voice you select. If you don't provide an engine, the standard engine is selected by default. If a chosen voice isn't supported by the standard engine, this will result in an error. For information on Amazon Polly voices and which voices are available for each engine, see Available Voices.

refs.Voice$SupportedEngines: Specifies which engines (standard, neural, long-form or generative) are supported by a given voice.

EngineNotSupportedException.base: This engine is not compatible with the voice that you have designated. Choose a new voice that is compatible with the engine or change the engine and restart the operation.

FlushStreamConfiguration.base: Configuration that controls when synthesized audio data is sent on the output stream.

refs.TextEvent$FlushStreamConfiguration: Configuration for controlling when synthesized audio flushes to the output stream.

refs.FlushStreamConfiguration$Force: Specifies whether to force the synthesis engine to immediately write buffered audio data to the output stream.

refs.Voice$Gender: The gender of the voice. Custom voices don't include this field.

refs.DescribeVoicesInput$IncludeAdditionalLan: Boolean value indicating whether to return any bilingual voices that use the specified language as an additional language. For instance, if you request all languages that use US English (es-US), and there is an Italian voice that speaks both Italian (it-IT) and US English, that voice will be included if you specify yes but not if you specify no.

InvalidLexiconException.base: Amazon Polly can't find the specified lexicon. Verify that the lexicon's name is spelled correctly, and then try again.

InvalidNextTokenException.base: The NextToken is invalid. Verify that it's spelled correctly, and then try again.

InvalidS3BucketException.base: The provided Amazon S3 bucket name is invalid. Please check your input with S3 bucket naming requirements and try again.

InvalidS3KeyException.base: The provided Amazon S3 key prefix is invalid. Please provide a valid S3 object key name.

InvalidSampleRateException.base: The specified sample rate is not valid.

InvalidSnsTopicArnException.base: The provided SNS topic ARN is invalid. Please provide a valid SNS topic ARN and try again.

InvalidSsmlException.base: The SSML you provided is invalid. Verify the SSML syntax, spelling of tags and values, and then try again.

InvalidTagParameterException.base: The resource ARN or a tag in the request isn't valid. Specify the ARN of a supported resource in the Amazon Web Services account and Region of the request. Tag keys can have a maximum length of 128 characters, and tag values can have a maximum length of 256 characters. Correct the ARN or the tags, and then try again.

InvalidTaskIdException.base: The provided Task ID is not valid. Please provide a valid Task ID and try again.

refs.CustomerManagedEncryption$KmsKeyArn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the key. The key must be a symmetric encryption key in the same Amazon Web Services Region as the voice. To create the voice, you need kms:DescribeKey, kms:GenerateDataKey, and kms:Decrypt permissions on the key. To synthesize speech with the voice, you need kms:Decrypt permission on the key.

refs.DescribeVoicesInput$LanguageCode: The language identification tag (ISO 639 code for the language name-ISO 3166 country code) for filtering the list of voices returned. If you don't specify this optional parameter, all available voices are returned.
refs.LexiconAttributes$LanguageCode: Language code that the lexicon applies to. A lexicon with a language code such as "en" would be applied to all English languages (en-GB, en-US, en-AUS, en-WLS, and so on.
refs.StartSpeechSynthesisStreamInput$Language: An optional parameter that sets the language code for the speech synthesis request. Specify this parameter only when using a bilingual voice. If a bilingual voice is used and no language code is specified, Amazon Polly uses the default language of the bilingual voice.
refs.StartSpeechSynthesisTaskInput$LanguageCo:
Optional language code for the Speech Synthesis request. This is only necessary if using a bilingual voice, such as Aditi, which can be used for either Indian English (en-IN) or Hindi (hi-IN).

If a bilingual voice is used and no language code is specified, Amazon Polly uses the default language of the bilingual voice. The default language for any voice is the one returned by the DescribeVoices operation for the LanguageCode parameter. For example, if no language code is specified, Aditi will use Indian English rather than Hindi.
refs.SynthesisTask$LanguageCode:
Optional language code for a synthesis task. This is only necessary if using a bilingual voice, such as Aditi, which can be used for either Indian English (en-IN) or Hindi (hi-IN).

If a bilingual voice is used and no language code is specified, Amazon Polly uses the default language of the bilingual voice. The default language for any voice is the one returned by the DescribeVoices operation for the LanguageCode parameter. For example, if no language code is specified, Aditi will use Indian English rather than Hindi.
refs.SynthesizeSpeechInput$LanguageCode:
Optional language code for the Synthesize Speech request. This is only necessary if using a bilingual voice, such as Aditi, which can be used for either Indian English (en-IN) or Hindi (hi-IN).

If a bilingual voice is used and no language code is specified, Amazon Polly uses the default language of the bilingual voice. The default language for any voice is the one returned by the DescribeVoices operation for the LanguageCode parameter. For example, if no language code is specified, Aditi will use Indian English rather than Hindi.

refs.Voice$AdditionalLanguageCodes:
Additional codes for languages available for the specified voice in addition to its default language.

For example, the default language for Aditi is Indian English (en-IN) because it was first used for that language. Since Aditi is bilingual and fluent in both Indian English and Hindi, this parameter would show the code hi-IN.

refs.Voice$LanguageName: Human readable name of the language in English.

LanguageNotSupportedException.base: The language specified is not currently supported by Amazon Polly in this capacity.

refs.LexiconAttributes$LastModified: Date lexicon was last modified (a timestamp value).

Lexicon.base: Provides lexicon name and lexicon content in string format. For more information, see Pronunciation Lexicon Specification (PLS) Version 1.0.

refs.GetLexiconOutput$Lexicon: Lexicon object that provides name and the string content of the lexicon.

LexiconAttributes.base: Contains metadata describing the lexicon such as the number of lexemes, language code, and so on. For more information, see Managing Lexicons.

refs.GetLexiconOutput$LexiconAttributes: Metadata of the lexicon, including phonetic alphabetic used, language code, lexicon ARN, number of lexemes defined in the lexicon, and size of lexicon in bytes.

refs.Lexicon$Content: Lexicon content in string format. The content of a lexicon must be in PLS format.
refs.PutLexiconInput$Content: Content of the PLS lexicon as string data.

refs.ListLexiconsOutput$Lexicons: A list of lexicon names and attributes.

refs.DeleteLexiconInput$Name: The name of the lexicon to delete. Must be an existing lexicon in the region.
refs.PutLexiconInput$Name: Name of the lexicon. The name must follow the regular expression format [0-9A-Za-z]{1,20}. That is, the name is a case-sensitive alphanumeric string up to 20 characters long.

refs.StartSpeechSynthesisStreamInput$LexiconN: The names of one or more pronunciation lexicons for the service to apply during synthesis. Amazon Polly applies lexicons only when the lexicon language matches the voice language.
refs.StartSpeechSynthesisTaskInput$LexiconNam: List of one or more pronunciation lexicon names you want the service to apply during synthesis. Lexicons are applied only if the language of the lexicon is the same as the language of the voice.
refs.SynthesisTask$LexiconNames: List of one or more pronunciation lexicon names you want the service to apply during synthesis. Lexicons are applied only if the language of the lexicon is the same as the language of the voice.
refs.SynthesizeSpeechInput$LexiconNames: List of one or more pronunciation lexicon names you want the service to apply during synthesis. Lexicons are applied only if the language of the lexicon is the same as the language of the voice. For information about storing lexicons, see PutLexicon.

LexiconNotFoundException.base:
Amazon Polly can't find the specified lexicon. This could be caused by a lexicon that is missing, its name is misspelled or specifying a lexicon that is in a different region.

Verify that the lexicon exists, is in the region (see ListLexicons) and that you spelled its name is spelled correctly. Then try again.

LexiconSizeExceededException.base: The maximum size of the specified lexicon would be exceeded by this operation.

MarksNotSupportedForFormatException.base: Speech marks are not supported for the OutputFormat selected. Speech marks are only available for content in json format.

MaxLexemeLengthExceededException.base: The maximum size of the lexeme would be exceeded by this operation.

MaxLexiconsNumberExceededException.base: The maximum number of lexicons would be exceeded by this operation.

refs.ListSpeechSynthesisTasksInput$MaxResults: Maximum number of speech synthesis tasks returned in a List operation.

refs.DescribeVoicesInput$NextToken: An opaque pagination token returned from the previous DescribeVoices operation. If present, this indicates where to continue the listing.
refs.DescribeVoicesOutput$NextToken: The pagination token to use in the next request to continue the listing of voices. NextToken is returned only if the response is truncated.
refs.ListLexiconsInput$NextToken: An opaque pagination token returned from previous ListLexicons operation. If present, indicates where to continue the list of lexicons.
refs.ListLexiconsOutput$NextToken: The pagination token to use in the next request to continue the listing of lexicons. NextToken is returned only if the response is truncated.
refs.ListSpeechSynthesisTasksInput$NextToken: The pagination token to use in the next request to continue the listing of speech synthesis tasks.
refs.ListSpeechSynthesisTasksOutput$NextToken: An opaque pagination token returned from the previous List operation in this request. If present, this indicates where to continue the listing.

refs.StartSpeechSynthesisStreamInput$OutputFo: The audio format for the synthesized speech. Currently, Amazon Polly does not support JSON speech marks.
refs.StartSpeechSynthesisTaskInput$OutputForm: The format in which the returned output will be encoded. For audio stream, this will be mp3, ogg_vorbis, ogg_opus, mu-law, a-law, or pcm. For speech marks, this will be json.
refs.SynthesisTask$OutputFormat: The format in which the returned output will be encoded. For audio stream, this will be mp3, ogg_vorbis, ogg_opus, mu-law, a-law, or pcm. For speech marks, this will be json.
refs.SynthesizeSpeechInput$OutputFormat:
The format in which the returned output will be encoded. For audio stream, this will be mp3, ogg_vorbis, ogg_opus, mu-law, a-law or pcm. For speech marks, this will be json.

When pcm is used, the content returned is audio/pcm in a signed 16-bit, 1 channel (mono), little-endian format.

refs.StartSpeechSynthesisTaskInput$OutputS3Bu: Amazon S3 bucket name to which the output file will be saved.

refs.StartSpeechSynthesisTaskInput$OutputS3Ke: The Amazon S3 key prefix for the output speech file.

refs.ServiceQuotaExceededException$quotaCode: The quota code identifying the specific quota.

Recording.base: A recording of the speaker whose voice you want to create. The recording specifies its audio format and its audio source.

refs.RecordingData$Bytes: The audio data, passed directly in the request. The data must be in the format that Format specifies and can be up to 5 MB. Amazon Polly doesn't store the audio after it creates the voice, and doesn't return this field in responses.

RecordingData.base: The audio source of a recording. In a CreateVoice request, specify exactly one of S3Url and Bytes. In a response, a recording that Amazon Polly read from Amazon S3 includes its S3Url. A recording that you passed as Bytes includes neither field, because Amazon Polly doesn't return the audio.

refs.Recording$Data: The audio source of the recording. Specify either an Amazon S3 object or the audio data.

refs.VoiceCreationData$Recordings: The recordings of the speaker. Each recording specifies its audio format and its audio source.

refs.StreamClosedEvent$RequestCharacters: The total number of characters synthesized during the streaming session.

refs.ConflictException$resourceId: The ID of the resource that the request conflicts with.
refs.ResourceNotFoundException$resourceId: The identifier of the resource that wasn't found.

ResourceNotFoundException.base: Amazon Polly can't find the specified resource. Verify that the resource exists in the Amazon Web Services account and Region of the request and that its ARN or ID is spelled correctly, and then try again.

refs.ConflictException$resourceType: The type of the resource that the request conflicts with.
refs.ResourceNotFoundException$resourceType: The type of the resource that wasn't found.

refs.RecordingData$S3Url: The Amazon S3 URL of the audio object, in the form s3://bucket/key. You need s3:GetObject permission on the object.

refs.StartSpeechSynthesisTaskInput$SampleRate:
The audio frequency specified in Hz.

The valid values for mp3 and ogg_vorbis are "8000", "16000", "22050", and "24000". The default value for standard voices is "22050". The default value for neural voices is "24000". The default value for long-form voices is "24000". The default value for generative voices is "24000".

Valid values for pcm are "8000" and "16000" The default value is "16000".

Valid value for ogg_opus is "48000".

Valid value for mu-law and a-law is "8000".
refs.SynthesisTask$SampleRate:
The audio frequency specified in Hz.

The valid values for mp3 and ogg_vorbis are "8000", "16000", "22050", and "24000". The default value for standard voices is "22050". The default value for neural voices is "24000". The default value for long-form voices is "24000". The default value for generative voices is "24000".

Valid values for pcm are "8000" and "16000" The default value is "16000".

Valid value for ogg_opus is "48000".

Valid value for mu-law and a-law is "8000".
refs.SynthesizeSpeechInput$SampleRate:
The audio frequency specified in Hz.

The valid values for mp3 and ogg_vorbis are "8000", "16000", "22050", "24000", "44100" and "48000". The default value for standard voices is "22050". The default value for neural voices is "24000". The default value for long-form voices is "24000". The default value for generative voices is "24000".

Valid values for pcm are "8000" and "16000" The default value is "16000".

Valid value for ogg_opus is "48000".

Valid value for mu-law and a-law is "8000".

refs.ServiceQuotaExceededException$serviceCod: The service code identifying the originating service.

ServiceFailureException.base: An unknown condition has caused a service failure.

ServiceQuotaExceededException.base: The request would cause a service quota to be exceeded.

refs.StartSpeechSynthesisStreamEventStream$Se: An exception indicating a service quota would be exceeded.

refs.LexiconAttributes$Size: Total size of the lexicon, in characters.

refs.StartSpeechSynthesisTaskInput$SnsTopicAr: ARN for the SNS topic optionally used for providing status notification for a speech synthesis task.
refs.SynthesisTask$SnsTopicArn: ARN for the SNS topic optionally used for providing status notification for a speech synthesis task.

refs.StartSpeechSynthesisTaskInput$SpeechMark: The type of speech marks returned for the input text.
refs.SynthesisTask$SpeechMarkTypes: The type of speech marks returned for the input text.
refs.SynthesizeSpeechInput$SpeechMarkTypes: The type of speech marks returned for the input text.

SsmlMarksNotSupportedForTextTypeExceptio.base: SSML speech marks are not supported for plain text-type input.

StartSpeechSynthesisStreamActionStream.base: Inbound event stream for sending input and control events to manage bidirectional speech synthesis.

refs.StartSpeechSynthesisStreamInput$ActionSt: The input event stream that contains text events and stream control events.

StartSpeechSynthesisStreamEventStream.base: Outbound event stream that contains synthesized audio data and stream status events.

refs.StartSpeechSynthesisStreamOutput$EventSt: The output event stream that contains synthesized audio events and stream status events.

refs.Voice$StatusReason: Additional information about the status of a custom voice. When the status is failed, this field describes why Amazon Polly couldn't create the voice.

StreamClosedEvent.base: Indicates that the synthesis stream is closed and provides summary information.

refs.StartSpeechSynthesisStreamEventStream$St: An event, with summary information, indicating the stream has closed.

SynthesisTask.base: SynthesisTask object that provides information about a speech synthesis task.

refs.GetSpeechSynthesisTaskOutput$SynthesisTa: SynthesisTask object that provides information from the requested task, including output format, creation time, task status, and so on.
refs.StartSpeechSynthesisTaskOutput$Synthesis: SynthesisTask object that provides information and attributes about a newly submitted speech synthesis task.

SynthesisTaskNotFoundException.base: The Speech Synthesis task with requested Task ID cannot be found.

refs.ListSpeechSynthesisTasksOutput$Synthesis: List of SynthesisTask objects that provides information from the specified task in the list request, including output format, creation time, task status, and so on.

refs.UntagResourceInput$TagKeys: The keys of the tags to be removed.

refs.CreateVoiceInput$Tags: The tags that you apply to the voice to help you categorize and organize it. Each tag consists of a key and an optional value, both of which you define.
refs.PutLexiconInput$Tags: The metadata that you apply to the lexicon to help you categorize and organize it. Each tag consists of a key and an optional value, both of which you define. Tag keys can have a maximum character length of 128 characters, and tag values can have a maximum length of 256 characters. You can't replace the tags of an existing lexicon by overwriting it with PutLexicon.
refs.TagResourceInput$Tags: The tags to add to the resource, as key-value pairs. Tag keys can have a maximum character length of 128 characters, and tag values can have a maximum length of 256 characters.

refs.GetSpeechSynthesisTaskInput$TaskId: The Amazon Polly generated identifier for a speech synthesis task.
refs.SynthesisTask$TaskId: The Amazon Polly generated identifier for a speech synthesis task.

refs.ListSpeechSynthesisTasksInput$Status: Status of the speech synthesis tasks returned in a List operation
refs.SynthesisTask$TaskStatus: Current status of the individual speech synthesis task.

refs.SynthesisTask$TaskStatusReason: Reason for the current status of a specific speech synthesis task, including errors if the task has failed.

refs.CreateVoiceInput$TermsAccepted:
Confirms the following two statements:

  • "I confirm that I have obtained all necessary consents required under any applicable laws and regulations, including biometric privacy laws, from the owner of this voice to clone these voice samples."

  • "I confirm that I will not use the generated content for any illegal, fraudulent, or harmful purpose and reaffirm my obligation to abide by the AWS Service Terms, Biometric Notice and Consent Terms, AWS Responsible AI Policy, and AWS Acceptable Use Policy."

You can read the AWS Service Terms, the Biometric Notice and Consent Terms, the AWS Responsible AI Policy, and the AWS Acceptable Use Policy on the Amazon Web Services website.

You must set this parameter to true to create a voice. Otherwise, the request fails with ValidationException.

refs.StartSpeechSynthesisTaskInput$Text: The input text to synthesize. If you specify ssml as the TextType, follow the SSML format for the input text.
refs.SynthesizeSpeechInput$Text: Input text to synthesize. If you specify ssml as the TextType, follow the SSML format for the input text.
refs.TextEvent$Text: The text content to synthesize. If you specify ssml as the TextType, follow the SSML format for the input text.

TextEvent.base: Contains text content to be synthesized into speech.

refs.StartSpeechSynthesisStreamActionStream$T: A text event containing content to be synthesized.

TextLengthExceededException.base: The value of the "Text" parameter is longer than the accepted limits. For the SynthesizeSpeech API, the limit for input text is a maximum of 6000 characters total, of which no more than 3000 can be billed characters. For the StartSpeechSynthesisTask API, the maximum is 200,000 characters, of which no more than 100,000 can be billed characters. SSML tags are not counted as billed characters.

refs.StartSpeechSynthesisTaskInput$TextType: Specifies whether the input text is plain text or SSML. The default value is plain text.
refs.SynthesisTask$TextType: Specifies whether the input text is plain text or SSML. The default value is plain text.
refs.SynthesizeSpeechInput$TextType: Specifies whether the input text is plain text or SSML. The default value is plain text. For more information, see Using SSML.
refs.TextEvent$TextType: Specifies whether the input text is plain text or SSML. Default: plain text.

ThrottlingException.base: The request was denied because of request throttling.

refs.StartSpeechSynthesisStreamEventStream$Th: An exception indicating the request was throttled.

ThrottlingReason.base: Provides information about a specific throttling reason.

refs.ThrottlingException$throttlingReasons: A list of reasons explaining why the request was throttled.

TooManyTagsException.base: The list of tags on the resource is over the limit. The maximum number of tags that can be applied to a resource is 50. Remove unused tags or reduce the number of tags in the request, and then try again.

UnsupportedPlsAlphabetException.base: The alphabet specified by the lexicon is not a supported alphabet. Valid values are ipa, x-sampa, x-amazon-pinyin, x-amazon-jyutping, x-amazon-pron-kana, and x-amazon-yomigana. Replace the unsupported alphabet with one of the valid values and resubmit your request.

UnsupportedPlsLanguageException.base: The language specified in the lexicon is unsupported. For a list of supported languages, see Lexicon Attributes.

ValidationException.base: The input fails to satisfy the constraints specified by the service.

refs.StartSpeechSynthesisStreamEventStream$Va: An exception indicating the input failed validation.

ValidationExceptionField.base: Information about a field that failed validation.

refs.ValidationException$fields: The fields that caused the validation error.

refs.ValidationExceptionField$message: A message describing why the field failed validation.

refs.ValidationExceptionField$name: The name of the field that failed validation.

refs.ValidationException$reason:
The reason the request failed validation. If Amazon Polly can't use the Amazon Web Services KMS key that you specified in CreateVoice, fields names CustomerManagedEncryption.KmsKeyArn and the reason is one of the following:

kmsKeyNotFound

No key with the specified ARN exists.

kmsKeyUnusable

The key is disabled, scheduled for deletion, or missing its key material, or it isn't a symmetric encryption key.

Voice.base: Describes a voice. Amazon Polly provides voices, and you can create custom voices with CreateVoice. Origin indicates whether Amazon Polly provides the voice or you created it. DescribeVoices returns a subset of the fields for each voice. GetVoice returns all fields of a custom voice.

refs.Voice$Arn: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of a custom voice, in the form arn:partition:polly:region:account-id:voice/voice-id. CreateVoice and GetVoice return this field. Voices that Amazon Polly provides don't have an ARN.

VoiceCreationData.base: The audio that you provide to create a custom voice.

refs.CreateVoiceInput$VoiceCreationData: The recordings that Amazon Polly uses to create the voice.
refs.Voice$VoiceCreationData: The data from which you created the custom voice. CreateVoice and GetVoice return this field. The response doesn't include the audio: a recording that Amazon Polly read from Amazon S3 includes its S3Url, and a recording that you passed as Bytes has no fields in Data.

refs.StartSpeechSynthesisStreamInput$VoiceId: The voice ID to use for the synthesis. To get a list of available voice IDs, use the DescribeVoices operation. To use a custom voice, specify the voice ID that CreateVoice returned, for example, vc-9a8fa85dd3. You can't specify the ARN of a voice.
refs.StartSpeechSynthesisTaskInput$VoiceId: The voice ID to use for the synthesis. To use a custom voice, specify the voice ID that CreateVoice returned, for example, vc-9a8fa85dd3. You can't specify the ARN of a voice.
refs.SynthesisTask$VoiceId: Voice ID to use for the synthesis.
refs.SynthesizeSpeechInput$VoiceId: The voice ID to use for the synthesis. You can get a list of available voice IDs by calling the DescribeVoices operation. To use a custom voice, specify the voice ID that CreateVoice returned, for example, vc-9a8fa85dd3. You can't specify the ARN of a voice.
refs.Voice$Id: The voice ID that Amazon Polly assigns. You specify this ID when you call the SynthesizeSpeech operation. For a custom voice, Amazon Polly assigns an ID that consists of vc- followed by hexadecimal characters, for example, vc-9a8fa85dd3.

refs.DescribeVoicesOutput$Voices: A list of voices with their properties.

refs.Voice$Name: The name of the voice, for example, Salli or Kendra. The name is human-readable, and you might display it in your application. For a custom voice, this is the Name that you specified in CreateVoice.

refs.Voice$Origin:
Indicates who provides the voice. The origin is one of the following:

aws

A voice that Amazon Polly provides.

customer

A custom voice that you created with CreateVoice.

refs.Voice$Status:
The status of a custom voice. Voices that Amazon Polly provides don't include this field. The status is one of the following:

pending

Amazon Polly is creating the voice.

active

The voice is ready for speech synthesis.

failed

Amazon Polly couldn't create the voice. StatusReason describes why.
